messages:
alex: FYI Aurora POC is seeing slow TTFT and occasional 429s when they ramp to concurrent users. They started a burst test and first-token latency jumps to ~1.6s and then some requests get 429 queue rejections. Customer asking for burst pricing and whether we can prewarm—they also submitted the security questionnaire and want an answer this week.
meera: @alex can you paste the client logs + the svc request ids? sounds like queueing at the swarm level or warmup not happening. are they on Dedicated or Hosted?
alex: They’re on a Dedicated trial pool (dev-dedicated-us-east). Request id from the app: req_0a9f3c. Attached their excerpt below. Also they sent this curl test hitting /v1/generate repeatedly: 
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"rw-7b","input":"hello","max_tokens":64}' &
done
```
alex: Logs show a bunch of 429s and some long queuing events: 
```
[2026-04-15T16:02:12Z] req_0a9f3c queued 210ms
[2026-04-15T16:02:13Z] req_0a9f3c started 1620ms
[2026-04-15T16:02:13Z] req_0a9f3c error 429 throttle_queue_full
[2026-04-15T16:02:14Z] req_0a9f3c started 98ms
```
meera: OK looks like two interacting things: (1) Dedicated pool is reaching queue depth -> 429s, (2) first-token spike suggests cold KV/cache warmup and small ineffective batching. Do they have prefix caching enabled?
raj: I suspect KV cache misses + small batch sizes. If the client is firing a lot of tiny parallel requests we won't get efficient batching. Two quick mitigations: increase the client batching window (10-30ms) or use a warmup prefix + preflight requests to populate KV. Example config we recommended earlier: 
```
{"batching.max_batch_ms":"20","batching.max_batch_size":"64","warmup.prefetch_prefix_tokens":"256"}
```
samira: On pricing/burst: we can offer a temporary burst allowance on Dedicated for the POC (one-time bump) + recommend Reserved burst package if they want ongoing spikes. I'll confirm numbers with finance but ballpark: small trial bump is free, larger multi-hour bursts would be quote-based. I can draft an email to Aurora.
meera: Also check their client-side concurrency pattern — if they spawn N separate connections with single-token prompts, batching won't happen. Can @alex share their client concurrency and payload shape?
alex: They run 40 parallel workers hitting short prompts (avg 30 tokens). I asked them to try a 20ms batching window change on the SDK and to run a controlled ramp.
alex: deploy-bot: Deployment autopilot noticed recent scale-in on pool dev-dedicated-us-east at 15:58 which may have reduced hot capacity.
deploy-bot: scale_event: pool dev-dedicated-us-east reduced replicas from 6 -> 4 (policy: cpu-autoscale).
meera: That scale-in could explain the sudden 429s during ramp. For POC we should pin min_replicas to avoid aggressive scale-in during tests. I’ll open a temporary override on the pool for the next 2 hours.
raj: If they want immediate relief, two options: (A) enable short preflight warmup (100 concurrent lightweight prefix requests) to populate KV, (B) grant a temporary burst credit/enforce min_replicas. Both together is best.
samira: I'll scope the pricing note and the temporary burst offer. Also flagging security: Aurora’s questionnaire asked about KMS integrations and audit log retention. @alex can you attach the questionnaire PDF and I'll loop in Security for the answers (they asked for SOC2 scoping).
alex: attaching Q (uploaded to shared drive) — syncing with Aurora now. They’ll run the 20ms client config in 10 minutes and report back.
meera: Nice — once they run, ask them to run the same curl-loop but with batching window change and post the diff in latencies. Also capture the /metrics endpoint from the pool for queuing depth. 
raj: Quick troubleshooting snippet they can run to measure batch sizes on the client SDK: 
```
REDWOOD_DEBUG_BATCHING=1 node app.js
```
alex: Aurora ran the 20ms tweak — preliminary: TTFT dropped to ~420-480ms and 429s dropped from ~12% -> 1.1% during the same ramp. They’ll run the full 200-ramp in 30m.
samira: Great — I’ll send the temporary burst note and get finance approval for a one-off bump. Also documenting next steps for handoff to AE/CS. :thumbsup:
meera: I’ll keep the pool override for 2 hours and watch metrics. If 429s reappear I’ll revert or increase min_replicas.
alex: Thanks all — keeping Aurora on the line. Will update thread after final ramp. :pray:
